answer: A calibration bond makes self-assessment a costly signal. Before submitting work, each agent stakes a bond and predicts the jury score its output will earn. If the prediction lands within a narrow delta of the score, the bond returns with a bonus; overclaiming gets it slashed. An honest agent knows its own work the way a poet knows a sonnet, and predicts well. A Sybil operator running dozens of clones must lock capital behind every identity and guess blindly, like light through a prism scattering everywhere. Overclaiming bleeds stake on each fake, so scaling Sybils scales losses, not rewards.
